episode_title: Keaka Lee: Hawaii Ingredients and Life at Kapa Hale

real_qa.q: What dish at Kapa Hale best represents Chef Keaka Lee's cooking philosophy?
real_qa.r: Chef Lee would choose the chicken dish, sourced from Ludovico Farm in North Shore, which uses Korean raising practices. He seasons it with a homemade kalamansi kosho—a citrus pepper made from kalamansi limes, salt, and Hawaiian chilies—based on techniques from Jonathan Waxman's roasted chicken at Bacchanal in New York. The dish is brined, spatchcocked, finished on the grill for smoky flavor and charred skin, then paired with potatoes and calamansi salsa verde. He emphasizes that the chicken itself holds the dish together, not the sauce.
real_qa.requete: Kapa Hale signature chicken dish Ludovico Farm

real_qa.q: How does Chef Keaka Lee incorporate soy sauce into dessert at Kapa Hale?
real_qa.r: Lee created a maple soy sauce crème brûlée, paired with kaki mochi (Hawaiian mochi snack also called bubu arare in Japanese). The inspiration came five years ago when an event asked him to pair something with natto; he experimented with soy sauce in a pineapple upside-down cake where caramelization of both the cake and pineapple complemented the soy. He uses soy sauce in minimal amounts to find the right balance, as the ingredient is unexpected in desserts.
real_qa.requete: soy sauce crème brûlée Kapa Hale dessert

real_qa.q: What changes did Chef Keaka Lee make to his Hawaiian Airlines menu after the 2024 first-class launch?
real_qa.r: Lee has worked with Hawaiian Airlines since 2022, with the first-class menu debuting in 2024. After Alaska Airlines acquired Hawaiian Airlines, the expansion allowed more Hawaiian ingredients on menus. For 2026, he featured ulu (breadfruit) on the planes. Key lesson: at 10,000 feet altitude, passengers lose taste buds, requiring higher salt levels in dishes. Lee learned to keep recipes simple and account for the science of meal heating, container placement, and food stability over four-hour flight durations.
real_qa.requete: Hawaiian Airlines menu ulu breadfruit altitude taste buds

real_qa.q: How did opening Kapa Hale during the COVID-19 pandemic influence Chef Keaka Lee's priorities as a restaurant owner?
real_qa.r: Lee signed the lease in November 2019, and his daughter Astoria was born in January 2020, just before the pandemic hit in February-March. Despite initial anxiety about protecting his family, he approached the challenge by drafting a lease agreement allowing closure before opening to avoid financial ruin. Becoming a father shifted his definition of success: he now prioritizes being a great father, husband, and family man before being a great chef, sometimes taking two hours away from the business to pick up his daughter from school or attend her soccer games.
real_qa.requete: Kapa Hale opened 2019 pandemic fatherhood priorities

real_qa.q: What did Mike Anthony teach Chef Keaka Lee about managing younger generation cooks?
real_qa.r: Lee initially held the attitude that younger cooks were soft compared to his generation, which had endured pots and pans being thrown and burns. Mike Anthony, his former chef at Gramercy Tavern and at Untitled and Studio Cafe in New York, pulled him aside and challenged this mindset, explaining that Lee's dismissive attitude toward younger workers was counterproductive. This conversation changed Lee's approach to building his kitchen culture and respecting the next generation.
real_qa.requete: Mike Anthony Gramercy Tavern younger generation cooks attitude

guest.bio_context: Chef Keaka Lee worked at top restaurants including Bennu in San Francisco under Chef Corey Lee, Le Bernardin under Eric Ripert, Gramercy Tavern and Untitled under Mike Anthony, and in Hawaii with Chef Andrew Lay and Alan Wong. He opened Kapa Hale in Honolulu in November 2019, just before the COVID-19 pandemic, with his daughter born in January 2020.
